title: Avimi son of Rachava of Pumbedita
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He and his brother Ifa were sons of Rachava, who married Chuma, described by Hyman as Rav Yehudah’s granddaughter, as in [Yevamot 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.64b.16). They were Rabbah’s students. [Shevuot 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.28b.9-11) has Ifa studying tractate Shevuot in Rabbah’s school (Rava’s school in Hyman’s quotation) when his brother Avimi met him and questioned him, then told him: “You have erred.” [Yerushalmi Nedarim 2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.2.3.2) and Shevuot 3:8 reverse this: Avimi says that he studied Nedarim and Shevuot, and Chifa wishes to test him. They were called “the sharp ones of Pumbedita,” as in [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.5), and appear under this name in [Kiddushin 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39a.2), or simply as “the sons of Rachava” in [Shabbat 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.103a.3) and [Sanhedrin 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.26a.6).[^3]

notes.text: The checked Shevuot passage reads Rabbah’s school, while Hyman’s quotation reads Rava’s. Ifa, Eifa and Chifa remain reported name forms. The opposite order in the Jerusalem Talmud is Hyman’s comparison.

The consulted Shevuot 28b has Eifa studying in Rabbah’s school, whereas Hyman’s quotation supplies Rava. Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 2:3 explicitly has Avimi, brother of Chifa, saying he studied Nedarim and Shevuot, and Chifa testing him. The reversed questioner direction is directly visible; the genealogy and teacher identifications remain Hyman’s.

Yevamot traces Chuma through Isi and Rav Yitzchak to Rav Yehudah and places her marriage to Rachava before her later marriages. Sanhedrin identifies Avimi and Eifa as sons of Rachava. Shevuot gives Rabbah’s school and makes Avimi test Eifa. Yerushalmi Nedarim makes Chifa test Avimi.
